chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Everything which flies, so there is no problem with its urine and its droppings.

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: so there is no problem (it is permissible/pure)

ai.seo_question: Are the urine and droppings of birds considered impure in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that the urine and excrement of flying creatures are ritually pure (*tahir*). This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the purity of surfaces contaminated by birds, reflecting the juristic principle that the waste of creatures with distinct biological characteristics (like flight) is treated differently from that of quadrupeds. It highlights the practical ease (*rukhas*) granted to believers in daily purification rituals.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Everything which flies, so there is no problem with its urine and its droppings’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Abd Allah ibn af-Mughirah from Jamil ibn Darraj from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Urine and droppings of the things that fly are not harmful.”’
